title: RBI Holds Rates at 5.25% as Oil Prices Cloud India's Inflation Outlook
excerpt: The central bank kept its policy rate unchanged in a unanimous decision, opting to wait for clearer inflation data as crude prices and a weak monsoon test Asia's third-largest economy.
body:
• The RBI's six-member monetary policy committee voted unanimously to hold the repo rate at 5.25%, retaining a neutral stance
  • The central bank cut its FY27 inflation forecast to 5% from 5.1% and slashed its core inflation estimate to 4.3% from 4.7%
  • GDP growth estimate was raised marginally to 6.7% from 6.6%, even as the RBI flagged monsoon shortfalls and geopolitical risks

Standing Pat While Peers Tighten

The Reserve Bank of India held its benchmark repo rate steady at 5.25% on Wednesday, choosing patience over preemptive action as it waits for clearer evidence on whether elevated oil prices are seeding broader inflationary pressures across the economy.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=qN443nUAkw0

The decision, unanimous among the six-member rate panel, sets India apart from a growing number of regional central banks — including Indonesia and the Philippines — that have responded to war-driven energy costs and currency volatility by tightening monetary policy. The RBI retained its policy stance at "neutral," signalling that its next move could go either way.

An overwhelming majority of 68 out of 72 economists polled by Reuters had correctly forecast the hold.

Inflation: Above Target but Not Alarming

Governor Sanjay Malhotra acknowledged that headline inflation has breached the RBI's 4% medium-term target, driven primarily by higher fuel prices. But he stressed that broader price pressures remain contained, reaffirming the central bank's "resolute" commitment to its inflation target.

"Inflation is expected to peak in the current September quarter before easing."

— Sanjay Malhotra, RBI Governor

The central bank trimmed its average inflation forecast for FY27 to 5% from 5.1% projected in June. More notably, the core inflation estimate — which strips out volatile food and fuel components — was cut to 4.3% from 4.7%, suggesting the RBI sees limited pass-through from energy costs to the broader price basket.

Retail inflation had risen above the 4% target for the first time in 17 months in June but remains within the RBI's tolerance band of 2% to 6%, giving policymakers breathing room.

Growth Holds Up, But Risks Loom

The RBI nudged its GDP growth estimate for FY27 upward to 6.7% from 6.6%, citing resilient domestic demand and a stronger-than-expected June quarter. However, Malhotra noted that a weak monsoon, trade disruptions, and geopolitical uncertainties could emerge as headwinds.

High-frequency indicators present a mixed picture. The purchasing managers' index has slipped to a five-year low, yet credit demand is growing at a robust 18% pace — a divergence that reflects an economy where manufacturing is sputtering even as consumption and investment hold up.

Brent crude, a critical variable for India as the world's third-largest oil importer, rebounded 2.9% to $86.2 a barrel on Tuesday, after sliding 7% in the previous session amid uncertainty over U.S.-Iran peace talks. Sustained high oil prices risk fanning inflation, widening the trade deficit, and squeezing corporate margins.

Markets Take It in Stride

Indian equities showed a muted reaction. The Nifty 50 slipped 0.03% to 24,607.20 while the BSE Sensex gained 0.42% to 78,756.07 by mid-morning. The benchmarks continued to display unusual divergence for the third consecutive session following the launch of a new closing-auction mechanism for stocks with futures and options contracts.

The rupee weakened marginally to 95.03 against the dollar, while the benchmark 10-year bond yield held flat at 6.7765%.

Broader markets fared better, with small-caps and mid-caps both rising and briefly touching all-time highs before the policy announcement.

What's Next

The RBI's wait-and-watch approach places a premium on incoming data over the next two months. If the monsoon deficit deepens and oil prices remain elevated, pressure to hike could build ahead of the October policy meeting. Conversely, if the U.S.-Iran diplomatic track produces a durable settlement that eases energy markets, the case for continued patience — or even resumed easing — would strengthen.

For now, the central bank has opted to preserve its optionality, signalling confidence in the economy's underlying resilience while keeping its powder dry for a potentially turbulent second half.
